svg.text: Explainable deep-learning analysis of an echocardiographic cine loop
Animated GIF of a dual-sector display; one still frame is
committed as frame_0.jpg. Sector rendering is schematic.
Green trace: ECG strip shown on the acquisition display.
42 frames read with a PIL seek loop until EOFError,
resized to 224 x 224 RGB, then preprocess_input.
metadata.csv - frame index, timestamp, width, height, filename.
A single row is committed in the repository.
VGG16 in the per-frame loop; ResNet50 in the Grad-CAM cell.
weights = imagenet; no cardiac fine-tuning is performed.

g.text: category, so the label space is not diagnostic:

svg.text: post hoc attribution, recomputed for every decoded frame

g.text: Gradient of the top-1 logit with respect to the last
region borders drawn by skimage mark_boundaries.
DeepExplainer with ten random background images;
channel-mean values on a diverging coolwarm map.

svg.text: 40 x 40 px patch, stride 40 (6 x 6 sweep); dashed outline = sector footprint
drop in the top-1 posterior when a patch is occluded

Figure 1 | Explainable-AI pipeline for an echocardiographic cine loop, as implemented in Echocardiogram_Data_Analysis.ipynb. (a) A single cine loop enters as an animated GIF; the exported still frame measures 2934 x 1189 px. (b) Frames are decoded with a PIL seek loop (42 frames), resized to 224 x 224 RGB and logged to metadata.csv. (c) An ImageNet-pretrained backbone is used without any cardiac fine-tuning, so (d) the top-1 posterior is an ImageNet-1k category rather than a diagnostic label. (e-h) Four post hoc attribution maps are then computed for each frame: Grad-CAM, LIME superpixels, SHAP DeepExplainer values and a 40 x 40 px occlusion sweep. Sector images, heat maps, stems and grids are schematic and report no measured performance.
